title: Run “Optimization suggestions” Console UX (beta): milestones, cohort, and success metrics
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Summary
Launch a new Redwood Console “Suggestions” view (beta) that turns Redwood Optimize batching/caching recommendation signals into an actionable, trustworthy UI. Beta is read-only behind feature flags + allowlisting; phase 2 adds “apply” workflows once we validate guardrails, rollbacks, and QA.

This ticket is the top-level PM driver for scope, milestones, beta cohort definition, success metrics, enablement plan, and go/no-go criteria.

## Problem
Customers (and CS/SE) can’t easily discover or trust cost optimizations today. The signals exist across telemetry + Optimize logic, but they are fragmented and require interpretation. We need:
- Clear suggestions with “what to change / why it helps / where it applies (route/model/region)”
- Standardized savings estimates with a transparent basis (not a black box)
- A risk taxonomy that supports safe adoption (latency/quality/SLO + reversibility)
- Telemetry contracts and instrumentation to measure adoption and realized impact

## Goals (beta)
1) Reduce time-to-value for Optimize by providing a first-class entry point in Console.
2) Increase adoption of batching/caching optimizations (starting with teams that have meaningful traffic + cost).
3) Build customer trust: explain “estimated savings” vs “guaranteed”, show confidence/assumptions, and surface concrete risk rationale.
4) Establish measurement loop: estimated vs realized savings and regression monitoring.

## Non-goals (beta)
- One-click apply (explicitly out of scope for beta GA; limited internal prototypes ok)
- Expanding beyond batching/caching to model swaps, quantization, routing policy recommendations
- Supporting every telemetry edge case on day 1 (we must fail safely + explain “insufficient data”)

## Target users / personas
- Platform/ML engineers optimizing production inference costs
- CS/SE/TAM during onboarding and quarterly optimization reviews
- (Secondary) Finance/ops stakeholders who want high-level savings visibility, but beta UI is still engineer-first

## Scope (beta)
### Product surface
- Suggestions list (table) with filters: route, model, region, rec type, risk level
- Detail drawer: summary + “how it works” + savings breakdown + risk rationale + “basis of estimate” (telemetry inputs)
- Empty states + “why no suggestions” troubleshooting guidance
- Read-only: no “apply” button, but include “How to implement” steps and links to docs

### Backend + contracts (at minimum)
- Suggestions list + detail endpoints with tenant scoping, pagination
- Savings estimate model: projected $/1M tokens + monthly impact (and CI/confidence score) + baselines
- Risk taxonomy (low/medium/high) with rationale bullets + auditable inputs
- Telemetry for impressions/opened and adoption measurement hooks (even if adoption is manual)

## Milestones / timeline (8–10 weeks)
Assume kickoff week of 2026-01-27.
- Weeks 1–2 (Discovery): finalize PRD + UX spec; lock beta cohort + enablement workflow; define success metrics + dashboards; confirm ADRs for risk + savings payload versioning.
- Weeks 3–6 (Build): implement data contract/APIs; Console UI (list + drawer + states); feature flags + allowlist tooling; initial telemetry events.
- Weeks 7–8 (Validation): offline eval validation of savings/risk; QA automation (gating/RBAC/schema); telemetry freshness + stale estimate detection; support playbook.
- Weeks 9–10 (Beta rollout): enable cohort gradually; weekly feedback + bug triage; publish docs; go/no-go for expanding cohort.

## Beta cohort (definition + selection criteria)
### Cohort size
- Initial: 6–10 workspaces (mix of Hosted + Dedicated; 1–2 Private/VPC if telemetry availability is confirmed)
- Expansion: up to ~25 workspaces after 2 weeks without major incidents/regressions

### Inclusion criteria
- Meaningful traffic on at least one route (enough volume for stable baselines)
- Prior expressed interest in cost optimization OR active Optimize usage
- Willingness to share qualitative feedback + join 30-min onboarding
- Has at least one operator who can implement batching/caching config changes (even manually)

### Exclusion / caution
- Highly irregular workload where baselines are unstable (unless explicitly a validation target)
- Tenants with incomplete metering/telemetry ingestion (we should not “guess”)
- Strictly regulated tenants where showing cost-derived usage patterns is a concern (requires explicit security sign-off)

### Enablement workflow
- Allowlist per workspace behind suggestions_beta flag
- RBAC: view permission required (no “everyone can see”) + audit logs of read access
- Rollback: immediate flag disable; no config changes are applied in beta

## Success metrics (beta)
### Adoption (leading indicators)
- % of allowlisted workspaces with at least 1 Suggestions visit/week
- Suggestion open rate (detail drawer opened per suggestion impression)
- “Trusted” signals: low bounce, repeated visits, CS/SE usage during onboarding, reduced support confusion

### Activation (implementation)
Because beta is read-only, we track “adopted” via:
- self-reported adoption during onboarding/check-ins + corroborating telemetry shifts (batch size/cache hit rate changes)
- optional internal tagging by CS/SE when customer confirms implementation

Targets (initial):
- 50% of cohort visits Suggestions in first 14 days
- 25% of cohort implements at least one recommendation within 30 days

### Outcome (lagging indicators)
- Estimated savings vs realized savings distribution (median absolute percentage error target: <= 30% on suggestions that are adopted; track by rec type)
- Realized cost reduction on affected routes (normalize for traffic changes)
- No material regressions:
  - p95 latency regression on affected routes: <= +5% for low-risk suggestions; <= +10% medium (unless explicitly accepted)
  - Quality regressions: within eval thresholds; no sustained increase in fallback/error rates attributable to the suggestion

### Reliability/Safety
- Suggestions-service p95 latency and error rate within SLO (final SLOs in ENG-2407)
- Stale estimate rate below agreed threshold; UI must clearly label “stale” and/or hide savings numbers when too old
- Zero tenant isolation incidents (P0)

## Go/No-go criteria for beta GA to cohort
Go if all are true for 5 consecutive business days in prod:
- Feature flag gating + allowlist verified, including rollback path
- RBAC checks + audit logging validated in prod
- No cross-tenant leakage; security review completed with mitigations
- Savings payload versioning stable; UI handles missing fields gracefully
- Support readiness: FAQ + escalation path + on-call runbook linked

No-go / pause beta if:
- Any tenant isolation or RBAC bypass incident
- Repeated stale baselines causing misleading savings display
- Evidence of recommendation-induced widespread latency/quality regressions

## Open questions (to resolve during weeks 1–2)
1) Confidence display: do we show a separate “confidence” field, or roll it into risk + “basis of estimate” narrative?
2) Savings estimate freshness: when do we hide numbers vs show with “stale” badge?
3) Double-counting prevention for caching + batching: final rule + how we message combined suggestions in UI.
4) Granularity: do we recommend at route+model+region always, or sometimes route-only?
5) Support model for beta: office hours cadence + expected response times; who triages estimation disputes?

## Latest updates
- 2026-02-06: Confirmed beta is read-only; phase 2 apply workflow will require explicit guardrails/rollback design + additional QA coverage. (See PM-413 for enablement/support readiness plan.)
- 2026-02-12: Security review flagged that savings/risk details can reveal usage patterns; mitigation: strict RBAC + audit logs + no export in beta.
- 2026-02-20: Early feedback theme: “High risk” label needs concrete reasons; ensure rationale bullets are always present in detail drawer and suppress suggestions when rationale is weak/under-specified.
